events.title: SILICON 2 GDS
events.description: Hands-on workshop exploring the complete ASIC design flow from RTL synthesis to GDSII layout generation using industry-standard Cadence EDA tools.
events.eligibility: All Engineering UG / PG students and Diploma scholars from ECE, EEE, EIE, and related branches.
rules: Participants must bring their college ID card for verification.
Participants are advised to bring their own laptops with charger; lab systems will also be provided on availability.
Strict attendance during both morning and afternoon sessions is mandatory for certificate entitlement.
[EVENT RULES WILL BE UPDATED]
procedure: Session 1: Introduction to RTL design, Verilog coding, and simulation verification.
Session 2: Synthesis with Cadence Genus, timing analysis, and constraints.
Session 3: Physical design, Floorplanning, Placement & Routing with Innovus.
Session 4: DRC, LVS checks and final GDSII export.
outcomes: Understand complete ASIC front-end to back-end flow.
Familiarity with industry-grade Cadence digital implementation toolchain.
events.certificates: Government-recognized Hardcopy Certificate of Workshop Participation will be awarded at the valedictory session.
importantInstructions: Reporting time at registration desk is 08:30 AM sharp.
Workshop participants cannot take part in other technical/non-technical events due to parallel full-day schedule.

faqs.q: Do I need prior experience with Cadence tools?
faqs.a: Basic knowledge of digital logic and Verilog is sufficient. The resource persons will guide you through the tool step-by-step.

faqs.q: Can I also attend technical events if I join this workshop?
faqs.a: No. Workshops run parallel full-day sessions, so workshop participants are restricted to this single workshop.

events.title: Embedded System
events.description: Comprehensive practical training on modern embedded architecture, peripheral interfacing, sensor integration, and real-time firmware development.
events.eligibility: Engineering & Diploma students interested in Embedded hardware and firmware.
rules: College ID card is compulsory.
Hardware kits will be provided for hands-on sessions during the workshop hours.
[EVENT RULES WILL BE UPDATED]
procedure: Session 1: Architecture overview of ARM Cortex & RISC-V microcontrollers.
Session 2: GPIO, Timers, ADC, and Interrupt handling in C.
Session 3: Interfacing communication protocols (I2C, SPI, UART).
Session 4: Mini practical project demonstration.
outcomes: Solid grasp of real-time embedded programming and hardware-software co-design.
events.certificates: Official Certificate of Workshop Completion from Mahendra Engineering College
importantInstructions: Bring your own laptop with Keil / Arduino IDE pre-installed if possible.

faqs.a: Yes, demonstration boards and sensor kits will be provided for lab exercises.

events.title: Virtual Instrumentation
events.description: Practical training on Graphical System Design, Virtual Instrumentation principles, signal acquisition, and automated test bench design using LabVIEW.
events.eligibility: All Engineering UG / PG students of Circuit branches (ECE, EEE, EIE, Mechatronics).
rules: Valid college identification required.
Participants must actively complete all four module exercises to receive certificates.
[EVENT RULES WILL BE UPDATED]
procedure: Module 1: Graphical programming fundamentals in LabVIEW (VIs, Front Panel, Block Diagram).
Module 2: Loops, Structures, Arrays, and Clusters.
Module 3: Data Acquisition (DAQ) hardware interfacing and signal conditioning.
Module 4: Real-time waveform display and instrument control.
outcomes: Proficiency in building automated measurement and control Virtual Instruments.
events.certificates: Accredited Hardcopy Workshop Certificate issued by ECE Department & VELOCITY Association.
importantInstructions: Full attendance is required across both sessions.

faqs.a: Yes, configured desktop systems with LabVIEW are provided in the department laboratory.

events.title: TECHPAPER
events.description: Platform to present innovative research papers in emerging domains including VLSI, Embedded Systems, IoT, Wireless Communication, AI/ML in signal processing, and Renewable Energy.
events.eligibility: UG / PG Engineering students. Teams must contain exactly 3 members.
rules: Every team must have exactly 3 participants (1 Team Leader + 2 Team Members).
Paper abstract must be submitted on or before 27/09/2026 via Google form provided in website itself.
Presentation time: 8 minutes for presentation + 2 minutes for Q&A by jury.
Slides should not exceed 10 slides. Standard IEEE paper format preferred.
[EVENT RULES WILL BE UPDATED]
procedure: Step 1: Submit abstract by 27/09/2026.
Step 2: Intimation of selected papers will be sent via email.
Step 3: Present before the panel on event day 08/10/2026.
Step 4: Evaluation based on novelty, technical depth, and presentation clarity.
perks: Attractive Cash Prizes for Top 3 Teams
Presentation Certificates to all team members
outcomes: Peer-reviewed feedback from veteran academicians and industry researchers.
events.certificates: Cash Prize with Winner Shields for Top Teams; Certificate of Presentation for all participants.
importantInstructions: carry softcopy in a pen drive.

faqs.q: Can members be from different colleges?
faqs.a: Yes, inter-college team members are allowed, but team size must be exactly 3 participants.

outcomes: Validate prototype viability and connect with innovation leaders.
events.certificates: Winner Cash Prize + Certificate of Excellence; Participation Certificates for all registered members.

events.title: TRACKTRON
events.description: High-speed autonomous line follower robotics challenge. Build and tune your robot to navigate tight curves, intersections, and speed checkpoints in record time.
events.eligibility: Open to all Engineering students. Team size must be exactly 3 participants.
rules: Team must have exactly 3 members.
The robot must be completely autonomous; no manual remote controls allowed.
Arena will have black lines (3cm width) on white background with 90-degree bends and speed sections.
Max dimensions: 25cm x 25cm x 20cm; max weight: 3kg.
[EVENT RULES WILL BE UPDATED]
procedure: Round 1: Calibration and qualifying time trial.
Round 2: Knockout obstacle track with checkpoints.
Fastest clean run with least penalties wins.
outcomes: Gain real-time robotics calibration, PID tuning, and sensor optimization skills.
events.certificates: Winner Cash Awards + Medals; Certificates of Technical Participation.
importantInstructions: Carry spare batteries and soldering kit if required for pit-lane repairs.

faqs.q: Can we modify robot code between runs?
faqs.a: Yes, during designated pit time before your official turn.

events.title: MIND MAZE
events.description: A fun-filled non-technical event where participants spin around an object and then attempt to solve a puzzle in a dizzy state, testing their focus and mental stability.
events.eligibility: Must be registered for at least one Technical Event with your 3-member team.
rules: Available only to participants who registered for a technical event.
The 3-member team competes together.
Use of mobile phones or internet search during the rounds is strictly prohibited.
[EVENT RULES WILL BE UPDATED]
procedure: Round 1: Circle the water can 5 times, run back and solve a simple picture puzzle in 60 seconds.
Round 2: Circle 10 times with an obstacle walk and solve a tougher jumbled puzzle while dizzy.
Round 3: 10 fast spins, zig-zag run and solve the final complex puzzle to become the Mind Maze Champion.
outcomes: Improves focus, balance and quick thinking under pressure while having fun.
importantInstructions: Report to the venue 15 minutes prior to scheduled start.

faqs.q: Can I register for Mind Maze without registering for a technical event?
faqs.a: No. As per symposium regulations, non-technical events can only be chosen in conjunction with at least one technical event.

events.eligibility: Must be registered for at least one Technical Event with your 3-member team.
rules: Available only for technical event registrants.
Teams will be provided specified challenges and must craft prompts using given AI models.
[EVENT RULES WILL BE UPDATED]
procedure: Challenge 1: Target image recreation through prompt refinement.
Challenge 2: Creative AI storyboarding and prompt efficiency.
outcomes: Master prompt engineering and generative workflow heuristics.
importantInstructions: Participants must do on there mobiles or laptop, systems will not be provided.

faqs.q: Which AI platforms will be used?
faqs.a: Standard open/accessible generative interfaces such as chatgpt, Gemini and more.
